notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/TextureTransformer entry, the sibling class that took the same route.

TextureSequence is the Animation child that plays a BTP_File against ModelComponents: Update forwards the fixed-point cursor; SetFile swaps the file and re-arms the base animation through dExtFrameCtrl_c::SetAnimation; Prepare is a static long-call veneer over func_02046d50. LoadFile (0x020178e4) and UpdateFileOffsets (0x020468a0) sit in other TUs' runs and stay their own shards.

The whole class folds, lifecycle variants included: the cartridge's D0,D1,C1 order is the order one ~TextureSequence() plus one TextureSequence() emits under deferred codegen (the emitted D2 and C2 siblings have no cartridge home and deadstrip unenrolled), so no per-variant shards remain.

SetFile stays a mangled extern "C" definition (wall 6az, notes/mwccarm-codegen.md): the Fix12<int> by-value parameter keeps the free spelling, and its call to dExtFrameCtrl_c::SetAnimation keeps the mangled spelling too because passing the real declaration's Fix12<int> by value homes the argument to the caller's stack. SetFlags, by contrast, takes a plain int and is spelled as the member call it is.
The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order under default deferred codegen; the emitted object carries the six functions ascending 0x0201597c..0x02015a7c.

The cartridge spells this class dExtAnmTexPat_c and its base dExtFrameCtrl_c (config/arm9/symbols.txt), so _ZTS/_ZTI records emitted under the project's TextureSequence/Animation spellings would have no configured ROM home. This TU therefore compiles with #pragma RTTI off, the same lever the TextureTransformer and MaterialChanger folds use for the identical dExt* coined-name situation: no RTTI records are emitted, and the vtable preamble's typeinfo word deadstrips with the rest of the .data output.
